$comment: Global sourcing registry for independent contest catalog construction. Every contest in the catalog must trace to a sponsor on this list, and a test enforces that. Organizations are grouped by tier: work top-down. `url_verified: true` means the URL itself was confirmed during research; the rest are the organization's known primary domain and should be confirmed on first use. READ `counts_are_estimates` BEFORE PLANNING A PASS.
sourcing_rule: NEVER populate a contest record from an aggregator. Only from the sponsoring organization's own published rules. If the sponsor's page cannot be found, the record stays unverified and does not ship.
counts_are_estimates: `estimated_total` on every org entry is a guess made before any of that sponsor's pages were read. It is NOT a target and it is NOT a denominator. Where a sponsor has actually been worked, verification has moved the number in both directions -- 10-10 was estimated at four QSO Parties and runs three; AGCW's ten includes one that publishes no closing time; NCJ's five dropped an SSB Sprint that no longer exists. `encoded` and `encoded_verified` are the real numbers, generated from the catalog by scripts/coverage.py and asserted by both test suites, so they cannot drift. Treat any gap between `encoded` and `estimated_total` as unexplored, not as work remaining.

field_notes.encoded: GENERATED. Contests from this sponsor currently in data/contests.seed.json.
field_notes.encoded_verified: GENERATED. Of those, how many carry verified:true -- rule read at the sponsor's own source.
field_notes.catalog_sponsors: Exact `sponsor` strings this org uses in the catalog. The join key. A sponsor string with no registry entry fails a test in both engines.
field_notes.status: complete | partial | blocked | not-started. `blocked` means a source problem that more effort will not fix -- read the note.

known_derived_sources.name: ARRL Contest Corral (monthly PDF)
known_derived_sources.reason: ARRL states the Corral is generated from data maintained on the WA7BNM Contest Calendar and extracted for QST. It is downstream of contestcalendar.com, not an independent compilation.

known_derived_sources.name: SM3CER Contest Service
known_derived_sources.reason: Third-party aggregator republishing sponsors' rules. Use it to FIND a sponsor's own site if needed, then source from the sponsor directly.

known_derived_sources.name: DXZone / hamradioworld / club news posts
known_derived_sources.reason: Downstream aggregators. Useful only for locating a sponsor's primary domain.

known_derived_sources.name: qrpcontest.com (QRP Contest Website)
known_derived_sources.reason: Two reasons, and the second is the one that settles it. It is an AGGREGATOR: a single page listing the contests of QRP ARCI, NAQCC, Flying Pigs, 4SQRP, ARS, AzScQRPions and NOGA, none of which it sponsors. And it links the WA7BNM Contest Calendar from its own front page, so it sits downstream of contestcalendar.com exactly as ARRL's Contest Corral does. Its own business is log submission -- 'all Contest Logs are submitted via an AUTOLOG' -- which is a service to those clubs, not authorship of their rules. THE MOST TEMPTING WRONG SOURCE IN THIS PROJECT: it states recurrences in precisely the form this catalog wants ('QRP ARCI Spring QSO Party, 2nd Saturday in April, 0000Z - 0600Z'), for the one sponsor whose rules are not on the public web at all. Taking them would look like sourcing and would be copying. Use it to learn that a contest EXISTS, then get the rule from the club. AND NOT LINKED, EITHER. Checked 2026-08-19: no catalog record references it in any field and no rendered page mentions it, which is the owner's call and the right one -- a calendar of other clubs' contests is not something this site sends readers to. That includes log_submit_url: it is the genuine log destination for several QRP clubs, so the temptation will recur, and if a sponsor's own rules direct logs there the answer is to say so in the record's note rather than to add the link.

known_derived_sources.name: NG3K Announced DX Operations (ADXO)
known_derived_sources.status: DISCOVERY ONLY -- NEVER A SOURCE OF DATES
known_derived_sources.reason:
Offered by the owner on 2026-08-23 as a reference, and it is a good one -- for the job an aggregator is allowed to do here. ADXO is the canonical list of announced DX operations and it carries each team's OWN website, which makes it the fastest way to learn an operation exists and where its primary source lives. That is exactly the use the sourcing rule permits, and the same standing SM3CER has: find the sponsor, then read the sponsor.

ITS DATES ARE NOT TAKEN, and RI1FJL is the case that shows why the line matters rather than being ceremony. ADXO shows that operation as 22-29 August. The team's own page gives a 7 August departure, a 6-7 day crossing and a 15-day operation, which puts them ashore around the 13th. A third report has them leaving on the 12th. Three numbers from three places, and only one of them is the team speaking. The record holds the team's figures, flags the start as unsettled, and says the announcement list disagrees -- which is more useful to a reader than silently picking whichever number looked confident.

Copyright W.B. Feidt 1996-2026. The page states no restriction on access, unlike WA7BNM, but that changes nothing about how it is used here.

known_derived_sources.name: DX-World
known_derived_sources.status: DISCOVERY ONLY -- NEVER A SOURCE OF DATES
known_derived_sources.reason:
Offered by the owner on 2026-08-23 alongside NG3K's ADXO, and it has the same standing: the best way to learn that an operation exists and to find the team's own site, and never the source of a date. DX-World is a news feed about DXpeditions, which means it is fast and it is also downstream of whatever the teams and the bulletins said -- exactly the position ARRL's Contest Corral occupies for contests.

DXZone was already listed here and still is. The owner named dxzone.com/catalog/DX_Resources/DX_Peditions/ in the same message; that is the same site under a different path and needs no separate entry, only the note that its DX catalogue is as useful for discovery as its contest pages and as unusable as a source.

tier_1_major_international.notes: Publishes a generic recurrence calendar in plain language, plus per-contest pages. Bands read at source 2026-08-16. Two records stay verified:false -- January VHF and 222 MHz And Up, whose recurrence was taken from the generic calendar rather than the contest's own page. KIDS DAY JANUARY ADDED 2026-08-23, unverified, and the hedge is ARRL's own: their page says 'GENERALLY the first Saturday in January' while the Generic Contest Calendar lists only the June running. The catalog had held June alone since the first seeding pass -- a gap inside a sponsor with 21 records, which is the gap audit's finding about bias WITHIN sponsors rather than only across them.

DONE 2026-08-16, all eight. CQ WW SSB/CW/RTTY, WPX SSB/CW/RTTY, CQ 160 CW/SSB, on five separate domains: cqww.com, cqwpx.com, cqwpxrtty.com, cqwwrtty.com, cq160.com. CQ PUBLISHES NO RECURRENCE RULE -- one sentence in the whole 2016-2026 corpus, in the 2016 WPX rules. Seven of the eight are held to CQ's own published dates and log deadlines instead; read data/sources.md, 'CQ publishes dates, not rules', before touching them. CQ 160 SSB is the FOURTH SATURDAY of February -- CQ's dates rule out 'last Saturday' in 2020 exactly as they rule out 'last full weekend' in 2026. Open: CQ has not published 2026 CQ WW rules, so CQ WW keeps a 5-day log deadline while the other three moved to 48 hours.

Excellent source, and the best-shaped one in the catalog for checking a rule: RSGB keeps a SEPARATE RULES PAGE PER YEAR at rsgbcc.org/hf/rules/{year}/r<slug>.shtml, so the sponsor's own published dates test the sponsor's own stated recurrence. Every record here is checked against four or five years of them. VHF contests live separately at /vhf/.

THE RULES INDEX IS A 403. rsgbcc.org/hf/rules/{year}/ refuses a directory listing, so pages have to be reached one at a time. Eleven were found by harvesting links out of /hf/results/results.shtml and the individual rules pages: rafs, rclubcalls, rhfchamp, riota, rnfd, r80mcc, rautumn, r160m, rallband_ft4, rcwc, rqrp. Several cover more than one contest -- rafs covers three, rnfd and r160m two each -- which is why a page count is not a contest count.

ENCODED SO FAR: IOTA; AFS CW, Datamodes and SSB (2026-08-19); and seven more on 2026-08-20 -- the February and November 1.8 MHz contests, National Field Day (CW), SSB Field Day, Club Calls, the Low Power Contest and the FT4 International Activity Day. That last one is the only unverified record of the eleven, and deliberately: RSGB ran it on the first Saturday of April in 2023, 2024 and 2025 and the SECOND in 2026, so no ordinal describes it and the record is manual, holding only the published date. Easter Sunday fell on 5 April 2026, which is a plausible reason and not a source.

TWO THINGS THIS PASS ESTABLISHED THAT LOOK LIKE STYLE AND ARE NOT. First, the AFS New Year exclusion does NOT generalise: 1 June 2024 was a Saturday and RSGB ran National Field Day on it, so NFD has no first-of-month exception even though its sibling does. Second, the two 1.8 MHz contests share one rules page but not one mode -- February is CW and SSB, November is CW only -- so they are two records, and both moved from 1900-2300 to 2000-2300 UTC in 2025 without the date rule changing.

STILL OPEN, and read but deferred: the Commonwealth Contest (BERU, page rcwc) -- its recurrence is clean, the second weekend of March, Sat 1000 to Sun 1000 CW, but the rules restrict entry by 'the Commonwealth Call Area from which they are operating' WITHOUT enumerating the areas anywhere on that page, so an entity_list would be this catalog's invention rather than RSGB's list. Also unread: the HF Championship (rhfchamp), the 80m Club Championships (r80mcc) and the Autumn Series (rautumn), all multi-leg series; the AFS 160 contest; and the four VHF/UHF AFS contests under /vhf/. estimated_total stays at 25 -- eleven pages covering at least sixteen HF contests, plus the multi-leg series and the VHF side, is still roughly that. HF CHAMPIONSHIP READ 2026-08-23 AND IS NOT A CONTEST: it is an award over eleven other contests, the same call already made about the WIA Contest Champion. It is however an excellent index of RSGB's season -- nine of its eleven were already encoded, and the two that were not are the UK/EI DX legs, now encoded under their own organiser. It also names the July contest 'International Low Power Contest', which settles half of the Low Power question in NEEDS_A_HUMAN. STILL OPEN: the 3.5 MHz Club Championship series (many legs, rotating CW/SSB/PSK63/RTTY, and the rules page says dates 'must be checked on the contest calendar' rather than listing them), the Autumn Series, AFS 160, and the four VHF/UHF AFS contests. THE TWO 80m SERIES ARE DONE, 2026-08-23. The 3.5 MHz Autumn Series (9 legs) and the 3.5 MHz Club Championship (18 legs) are encoded as three records each, split by mode, using per-date times -- both series move their clock mid-run and the Club Championship's dates are not on its rules page at all: RSGB publishes them on a CGI calendar at cgi-bin/hfreadcal.pl?year=YYYY and the rules page links to it. That calendar is the answer to 'where are RSGB's dates' generally and is worth reading first next time. STILL OPEN: AFS 160, the four VHF/UHF AFS contests, and the Eclipse contests the calendar lists in August, which are new and unread. RSGB IS EFFECTIVELY DONE ON HF, 2026-08-23. Reading its CGI calendar end to end closed the remaining gaps and settled three questions. AFS 160 IS NOT A SEPARATE CONTEST -- the calendar labels the 14 November entry 'Club Calls (1.8MHz AFS)', which is the Club Calls record already held. The RSGB FT4 Contest Series (12 Monday legs, clock shifting for the summer) and both ECLIPSE contests are now encoded; the Eclipse pair carries active_until 2026 because RSGB describes them as tied to the 12 August 2026 eclipse specifically, which is what that field means and is a different state from the manual records awaiting next year's dates. TWO THINGS ON THAT CALENDAR ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CONTESTS: the HF Championship and the GR2HQ Challenge are both AWARDS over other contests -- GR2HQ is entered by registering rather than by submitting a log -- and the WIA Contest Champion set that precedent. STILL OPEN: the Commonwealth Contest, deferred on eligibility rather than on reading, and the four VHF/UHF AFS contests, which live on a different calendar under /vhf/. COMMONWEALTH ENCODED 2026-08-23 and the deferral is closed. It sat for three days on ELIGIBILITY rather than on reading: the rules limit entry to 'the Commonwealth Call Area list' and the rules page does not print it, so an entity_list would have been this catalog's invention wearing RSGB's name. RSGB DOES publish it, at hf/information/codes.shtml, linked from the rules page -- the blocker was a link nobody had followed, which is worth remembering the next time a record is deferred for a missing list. 143 call areas, 151 prefixes, read from that page. RSGB IS NOW COMPLETE ON HF; only the four VHF/UHF AFS contests remain, and they are a different referat under /vhf/.
HF World Championship administered by ARRL and encoded. Region 1 contests (Field Day CW/SSB, 50/145 MHz, 70 MHz) via iaru-r1.org -- not started.

SOURCED 2026-08-18 from darc.de/der-club/referate/conteste/ -- the last unworked tier-1 org. Eight encoded: WAE DX CW/SSB/RTTY, WAG, the 10m Contest, the Weihnachtswettbewerb, and the quarterly FT4 and RTTY-Kurzcontest series. Every date and every log deadline was checked against DARC's own "Termine DARC KW Conteste 2026" table at /darc-kw-conteste/kw-conteste/, which is the registered url. estimated_total now counts the HF contests DARC runs itself and lists there: the five not encoded are the Ostercontest, the Hell Contest, the HELL-Kurzcontest, the Ausbildungscontest and the CW-Ausbildungscontest. The IARU Region 1 Fieldday appears on that table but is IARU's event, not DARC's -- same call as UBA. DARC's UKW/VHF contests are a separate referat and are not counted here.

Sourced 2026-08-17 and finished 2026-08-19. All eight of JARL's own contests are encoded. The four English-indexed ones came first -- All Asian DX (CW and Phone legs), JARL WW RTTY and the New Year QSO Party. THE FOUR JAPANESE-LANGUAGE ONES ARE NOW READ: ALL JA, 6m AND DOWN, Field Day and 全市全郡 (ACAG), each from its own 規約 page, which states the recurrence in a numbered clause and then prints that year's dates separately at the head of the page -- an independent check on the same document. Times are encoded as Asia/Tokyo wall clock because JARL writes 21時00分（JST）; Japan has had no daylight saving since 1952, so the instant never moves, and a test says so. ACAG is the catalog's only rule anchored on a public holiday and counted backwards -- two days before Japan's Sports Day, the second Monday of October -- and that is not cosmetic: a 'second full weekend' reading moves it a whole week in 2028 and 2029. All four are Japan-only for ENTRY ('日本国内のアマチュア局およびSWL') and carry no log_deadline_days: JARL prints a dated deadline per edition rather than a span, the same reason its All Asian records carry none.

Sourced 2026-08-17. Remembrance Day, John Moyle Memorial Field Day, VK Shires, Harry Angel Memorial Sprint, Trans-Tasman Low-Band. Each has its own rules page under /members/contests/. Remembrance Day is the one contest in the catalog needing the nearest_weekday rule ('weekend in August closest to the 15th'). WIA's Oceania DX page is a co-sponsor's statement of the OCDX recurrence and is cited as such by those two records; the contest itself belongs to the Oceania DX Contest Committee in tier 3. WIA's Harry Angel page contradicts itself on 2027 -- the rule is thrice-stated and is what the record follows; the discrepancy is in that record's note. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: THIS WAS MARKED COMPLETE AT 5 OF 5 AND IT WAS NOT. WIA's own nav lists ten 'Official WIA Contests', and three of them were unencoded: the Australia Day Contest, the Ross Hull Memorial VHF/UHF Contest (Marathon) and the VHF-UHF Field Days. Australia Day is now encoded -- 26 January, opening 2200 UTC on the 25th, which is 0900 on the 26th in eastern Australia. THE OTHER TWO ARE READ BUT NOT ENCODED, and the blocker is tooling rather than source. Both pages state their recurrence plainly -- Ross Hull is 'the month of January', and the Field Days are the 1st full weekend of January, the 3rd weekend of June and the 3rd weekend of September, all 0100 UTC Saturday to 0059 UTC Sunday -- but neither page carries a BAND LIST, deferring to a rules PDF, and those PDFs yield no text to the extractor used in this pass. A human with a PDF reader gets the band list in seconds. Do not encode them with guessed bands. Of the remaining nav entries, the Commonwealth Contest is RSGB's BERU and the Contest Champion is an award over WIA's other contests, so neither is a WIA contest to encode; the estimate of 8 counts the ten minus those two.

Sourced 2026-08-17; the catalog's first non-US North American contests. RAC runs two: Canada Day (fixed to July 1) and Canada Winter. The stub's third was a duplicate of the second. Canada Winter is the project's best-evidenced `manual` record -- eight dates from eight of RAC's own annual rules PDFs, fitting no ordinal Saturday, and a Sunday in 2026. Rules are published as a fresh PDF each year whose path embeds the upload month, so rules_url is this stable hub instead.

ADDED 2026-08-21 from the gap audit, and the reason it was missing is the point of that audit: WWROF appeared NOWHERE in this registry, so the World Wide Digi DX Contest was never a candidate for verification. It is a major FT4/FT8 contest running since 2019 and squarely in the modes this catalog claims to cover. The 221-of-229 verification rate measured the accuracy of what had been listed and said nothing about what had never been listed. Sponsor states the recurrence in words on its front page and keeps per-year rules PDFs, so the rule is checkable against the sponsor's own dates -- 2024, 2026, 2027, 2028 and 2029 all reproduce. WWROF also co-sponsors other events; this entry covers WW Digi only, and estimated_total should be revisited if that changes.

Both legs encoded 2026-08-23 from jidx.org's own English rules page, which states one rule covering both: 2nd full weekend of April for CW and of November for Phone, 0700 Saturday to 1300 Sunday, 1.8 through 28 MHz, prefecture number from JA and CQ zone from everyone else. Separate from JARL, which has its own entry and its own contests -- JIDX is run by its own committee.

SOURCED 2026-08-18. Coupe du REF CW/SSB, REF 160 Metres, DDFM 50 MHz -- four records, all from REF's own French-language rules PDFs, each tested against two years REF published independently. Still open: the Championnat de France THF, deferred because no REF document consulted states its modes and a record with no mode fails a catalog test. SOURCED 2026-08-18. Estimate raised from 10. UBA's contest calendar is an aggregator except for rows marked (**), which UBA labels 'see: HF > Contest Rules' -- its own events -- and only those rows were used, as a second published source for dates. The BMA page points to belgianmillaward.be for the complete rules; only UBA's own page was used.

SOURCED 2026-08-18. PACC and PACCdigi. URL corrected -- the registry's 'commissies-werkgroepen/traffic-bureau/pacc-contest/' path 404s; the live tree is 'commissies-en-werkgroepen/traffic-bureau/hf-contesten/'. SOURCED 2026-08-18. SP DX Contest only. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The registry's spdxcontest.info is no longer this contest's site -- the domain now serves an unrelated adult-site directory. The sponsor's own site is spdxcontest.pzk.org.pl, with per-year rules at /<year>/rules.php. (2) The SP DX RTTY Contest is not this org's: its rules name PK RVG, the Polish Radiovideography Club, as organiser. It now has its own entry.

Its SP DX RTTY Contest was previously assumed in this registry to belong to PZK / SP DX Club; the rules name PK RVG as organiser ('The SPDX RTTY Contest organized the Polish Radiovideography Club (PK RVG)') with PZK as a co-sponsor, so the contest is recorded here instead.

SOURCED 2026-08-18. OK/OM DX SSB and CW (sponsor string 'CRK / SARA') and the OK DX RTTY Contest (sponsor string 'CRK'), which is registered here under the same org because it is hosted on crk.cz and takes logs at okrtty@crk.cz -- but neither its English nor its Czech rules page names an organising society, so the attribution is an inference and the record says so. BLOCKER, not transient: okomdx.crk.cz and okrtty.crk.cz both serve a TLS certificate issued for default.web4u.cz, so HTTPS fails validation. Both rules_url values are http:// deliberately and the link checker will keep reporting them until CRK fixes the hosts.

SOURCED 2026-08-18. ARI International DX, Contest delle Sezioni HF, ARI 40/80 -- three records, from ARI's own Italian rules PDFs and its 40/80 rules page. URL corrected: ari.it/contest-hf/ari-international.html carries results, not rules; the rules live at contest.ari.it/hf_web/rules/*.pdf, indexed at regolamenti.php. Still open: the Marconi Memorial HF Contest, which is on ARI's calendar for 4-5 July 2026 but has no rules page on ari.it, and Marconi Club ARI Loano, a separate body. Coppa ARI was struck from the estimate: it is a trophy awarded on combined placings in the two contests above, not a contest of its own -- the same call made for AGCW's Goldene Taste. ari.it's contest calendar is an aggregator and was not used.

SOURCED 2026-08-18. All six of URE's HF contests: King of Spain CW and SSB, EA RTTY, EA PSK63, CNCW and CME. The last two run two sessions with an overnight break and use the sessions array. CONTRADICTION IN URE'S OWN PAGES: the 'Annual HF Championship Rules 2026' page lists every one of the six a day later than the individual rules pages do, and each of its dates is a 2025 weekend -- so it was not used as an independent date source. The individual pages are self-consistent for 2026 and are what is encoded. EA-QRP CW, listed in the previous estimate, is not on concursos.ure.es.

SOURCED 2026-08-19, and Tier 2 is now 21 of 21 worked. Three records, all from REP's own rules pages: the Portugal Day Contest on HF, the Portugal Day VHF/UHF contest and the REP 50 MHz contest. URL corrected -- rep.pt itself carries no rules; its front page links concursos.rep.pt, which is REP's contest portal, and the HF rules are mirrored at portugaldaycontest.rep.pt. REP PUBLISHES TWO CONTRADICTORY VHF/UHF RULES AND BOTH ARE LIVE: concursos.rep.pt says 10 June (the holiday) every year with 2m/4m/70cm/23cm/13cm and a 20 June log deadline, while portugaldaycontest.rep.pt/regras_vhf_uhf.php still says the second Saturday of June with 2m/70cm/23cm and a 30 June deadline. The fixed date is encoded because REP ran it on Tuesday 10 June 2025 -- its own logs-received post is dated that day -- and the second Saturday of June 2025 was the 14th. NOT ENCODED: the REP FT4 contest, which REP publishes as three dated editions with two different clock windows (22 Feb 2025 2000-2100 UTC, 18 Apr 2025 and 18 Aug 2025 both 2100-2200 UTC) and no recurrence. A manual record carries one start/end pair for all its dates, so this series cannot be stated exactly without either splitting one contest into three records -- misrepresenting REP's own framing -- or adding per-date times to the schema. No 2026 edition has been published. It is read and documented in data/sources.md rather than approximated. The estimate of 3 named 'Portugal Day Contest, Navy Day'; there is no Navy Day contest anywhere on REP's site, and the real programme is these three plus FT4, so the estimate is corrected to 4. REP's 4m (70 MHz) band is in its VHF/UHF band list but not in this catalog's band vocabulary, so it is recorded in bands_note. If a fourth record ever needs it, adding 4m to CATALOG_BANDS in both engines is the fix.

Helvetia Contest, Field Day CW and SSB, National Mountain Day, Weihnachtswettbewerb SSB and CW. That is the whole KW-Contest programme, counted from USKA's own page rather than guessed. The Reglemente are PDFs linked from /kw-contest/, which also prints the year's dates independently and is what every record is tested against.

CORRECTED 2026-08-23, AND THE OLD ENTRY WAS RIGHT ABOUT ITS SCOPE AND WRONG ABOUT THE ORGANISATION. nrau.net really does say 'All NRAU Contest related information is under revision' and really does publish nothing usable for NRAU-Baltic or the Nordic Activity Contests -- that part stands and those three are still unencoded. But NRAU also organises the SCANDINAVIAN ACTIVITY CONTEST, its flagship and one of the oldest in Europe, which publishes complete rules at sactest.net including standing recurrence wording for both legs. SAC appeared NOWHERE in this registry until the gap audit -- not under NRAU, not as an entry of its own, not in anyone's estimated_total. Both legs are now encoded: CW on the 3rd full weekend of September, SSB on the 2nd full weekend of October, 1200Z Saturday to 1159Z Sunday. THE LESSON IS THE GENERALISABLE PART: a blocked organisation stopped being asked what else it runs. CRAC, SRS, FRR and IARC Holyland deserve the same question. BLOCKED at source. nrau.net says 'All NRAU Contest related information is under revision', and no NRAU-Baltic rules are published anywhere on the site. The NAC / Nordic Activity Contest pages give dates and times but state no modes and link no rules, so a record built from them could not declare a mode and would be dropped silently by every mode filter. Nothing encoded; the five NAC recurrence rules and the 19:00-23:00 local-time finding are recorded in data/sources.md for when NRAU republishes. The national societies SSA (SE), NRRL (NO), EDR (DK) and SRAL (FI) are separate work.

Six encoded across the three societies: LRAL's 18 November and 4 May 80m contests, ERAU's ES Open HF Championship and ES LL KV series, LRMD's Vytautas Magnus Contest and WAL Contest. Each society is its own catalog sponsor -- LV, EE and LT records are not interchangeable -- and each has its own site: lral.lv, erau.ee, lrmd.lt. The joint NRAU-Baltic Contest is blocked at NRAU, not here.

Russian DX Contest encoded, and only for 2027: rdxc.org publishes a date rather than a recurrence rule, and the only edition currently announced is 20-21 March 2027. RAEM, Russian 160m, the Russian WW series and the RCC Cup are on separate hosts and have not been read.

The three 2026 HF championships (RTTY, CW, SSB) and the Low Power Cup encoded, all from UARL's own reglamenty. CORRECTION: https://uarl.org.ua/ fails TLS certificate validation; http:// serves the site, so the registry records the http URL. UKEICC publishes three years of dates and no recurrence, and the SSB leg proves the absence is real rather than an omission: 1st Saturday of November, then 5th of October, then 4th. tier_3_other_regions.notes: UNBLOCKED AND SOURCED 2026-08-19, after being the catalog's longest-standing blocker. THE LEAGUE HAD MOVED. sarl.org.za served an expired TLS certificate in August 2026 and is now worse than that -- it answers on http with a cPanel 'Default Web Site Page', i.e. a parked domain, so it was never coming back. The SARL is at mysarl.org.za, and contest.sarl.org.za redirects there. WHAT IT PUBLISHES: an 84-page 2026 SARL Contest Manual (Version 1.1, 2025-12-15) plus a per-contest rules PDF for each major event, AND its own SARL-Contests-2026-Calendar.ics with 53 events. The .ics is the independent second source every record is tested against; its times carry TZID='South Africa Standard Time', a fixed +0200 with no DST, and SARL's own X-CALSTART confirms the offset by writing 09:00 local as 07:00Z. TWENTY-ONE RECORDS ENCODED: the HF Phone, Digital and CW contests (1st, 2nd and 4th Sundays of August), the National Field Day (two legs, one record), the Africa All Mode International DX Contest, the Africa FT4 DX Contest (two legs, one record) and the two Equinox 6m challenges (two records, because their end offsets differ). A GUESS THIS CORRECTED: the sarl-hf-phone record had been carried unverified with eligibility guessed as ZS-only and a note saying 'Confirm'. It is worldwide -- the scoring table's Area 9 is 'Stations in the rest of the world' -- and both Africa DX contests say so outright. Its bands were also empty for want of a readable source and are now recorded, which leaves jarl-new-year-qso-party as the catalog's only bands: [] record. THE REST OF THE PROGRAMME FOLLOWED the same day, read from the Contest Manual once the per-page font decoding worked: the four QRP legs, the three Club Contests, the 80 m QSO Party, the YL, Youth and Newbie QSO Parties, the HAMNET 40 m Simulated Emergency Contest and the Top Band QSO Contest. THE VHF/UHF FM MODE CONTEST IS NOW ENCODED TOO, and it is the record that put FM into this catalog's mode vocabulary: it is FM only, and there was no FM token, so recording it would have meant calling it SSB. STILL OPEN: the Youth of the Air Contest, whose only PDF on the site is the 2024 edition and which does not appear in the 2026 Contest Manual at all -- so it may simply not run any more. Ask SARL rather than assume either way. ONE RECORD IS DELIBERATELY UNVERIFIED: the Top Band QSO Contest. SARL's prose and its own date table disagree about the start day, and 'the first full week of June' has two readings that agree in 2026 and diverge in 2027. It is encoded as manual with SARL's published 2026 date only, and asking SARL which reading is intended turns it into a rule. The .ics also carries events run by OTHER South African bodies -- the Antique Wireless Association, HamSat-SA, the ZS1-ZS5 provincial QSO parties -- which are separate sponsors and separate work.

Sourced 2026-08-17. Added as its own org because the OCDX Contest is run by a joint VK/ZL committee, not by the WIA or NZART -- 'The Oceania DX (OCDX) Contest is managed by the Oceania DX Contest Committee.' Its country is OC, the one non-national code in region_map, because no single country's society owns it. NOTE ON PROVENANCE: the committee's PDF states only the current year's dates, so the recurrence in words is cited from co-sponsor WIA's Oceania page. That is a sponsor, not an aggregator, and the two records say so.

Jock White Memorial Field Day, Sangster Shield, Memorial Contest, and the ZL Autumn and Winter Sprints as three records -- NZART runs CW, SSB and FT4 in three back-to-back 29-minute windows and scores each separately. BLOCKED -- THE RULES ARE IMAGERY. Checked 2026-08-17. GACW moved to gacw.ar and its WWSA page carries only two PDFs, WWSA_Reglas_Castellano.pdf and WWSA_Reglas_Ingles.pdf. SOURCED 2026-08-19. The stub guessed four contests -- 'TRC DX, TRC Digi, TA VHF/UHF, Turkey HF'. TRAC publishes ONE: the TA VHF-UHF Contest, with a page per year back to 2021 and a scores page per year. There is no TRC DX, TRC Digi or Turkey HF contest anywhere on trac.org.tr; the estimate is corrected to 1. The site's other contest-shaped link, ta-vhf-cqww, is a how-to for exporting a TA contest log into CQ WW VHF, not a TRAC contest. THE ONE RECORD IS verified: false ON PURPOSE. TRAC's rule -- 'Temmuz ayının ilk hafta sonu', the first weekend of July -- reproduces its published 2024, 2025 and 2026 dates but not 2023, when 1 July was itself a Saturday and TRAC ran the contest a week later on 8-9 July. exclude_dates [[7,1]] fits all four dates and is this catalog's inference, not TRAC's wording. It bites again in 2028, 2034 and 2045. One question to TRAC settles it.

tier_3_other_regions.org: South African club contests (via the SARL Contest Manual)
tier_3_other_regions.notes: ADDED 2026-08-19. Nine contests run by nine South African clubs, one each, all sourced from the 2026 SARL Contest Manual. ONE ENTRY RATHER THAN NINE because they share a single source, the same way the Baltic trio shares one -- but each club is its own catalog_sponsors string, because a Cape Town record is not a Durban one. THE MANUAL IS A PRIMARY SOURCE FOR THESE, AND THE REASONING MATTERS. It carries each contest's FULL rules -- aim, dates, exchange, frequencies, scoring, log sheets -- and names its organising club, rather than summarising a calendar entry. It is the venue in which South African clubs publish their rules, as DARC's Ausschreibungen and UBA's rules pages are for theirs. An aggregator republishes rules it found elsewhere; this is where the rules appear. ELIGIBILITY IS UNVERIFIED ON SEVEN OF THE NINE. The manual states no participation clause for the provincial parties, the Hammies party or the Early Morning Coffee party, and there is no blanket clause in the general rules. Their scoring contemplates stations outside the region, so they are recorded worldwide with verified false -- an absence of words, not a statement. ALL THREE REMAINING ONES ARE NOW ENCODED, taking this entry to 12 of 12: the PEARS National VHF/UHF Contest (two 22-hour sessions off a 2nd-Friday-of-January anchor, which is what the sessions array is for), the AWA Valve SSB QSO Party, and the ZS SOTA Activity Weekend. The SOTA record is the catalog's SECOND with no bands: SARL states 'All amateur bands and modes', so there is no list to record and inventing one would be writing a restriction SARL did not. It is also the one that sits closest to the edge of what this catalog is for -- scored through the SOTA database rather than by a log to the sponsor -- and its note says so. BACAR appears in SARL's news categories but has no rules in the manual.

BLOCKED -- NOT AN AGGREGATOR PROBLEM, A SOURCE PROBLEM. qrparci.org/contests carries prose only ('We sponsor several contests each year with the emphasis on having fun!'); qrparci.org/qrp-event-calendar renders nothing without JavaScript and exposes no data endpoint; the site's WordPress page list contains exactly one 'contests' page and no per-contest rules pages. Rules appear to live in the members' magazine QRP Quarterly. qrpcontest.com is NOT a source and the earlier description of it here was too generous: calling it 'a third-party logging service' understates the problem. Re-read 2026-08-19 -- it is an aggregator listing seven clubs' contests, none of which it sponsors, and it links the WA7BNM Contest Calendar from its own front page, so it is downstream of contestcalendar.com exactly as ARRL's Contest Corral is. It now has its own known_derived_sources entry and a test in both engines. It is also the most tempting wrong source in this project, because it states QRP ARCI's recurrences in precisely the form this catalog wants ('2nd Saturday in April, 0000Z - 0600Z') for the one sponsor whose rules are nowhere on the public web. Taking them would look like sourcing and would be copying. NO RECORDS CREATED, deliberately: eight estimated, zero encoded, and that gap is the sourcing rule working rather than work outstanding. Next step needs a human. QRP ARCI's own Contact Us page names Larry Makowski W2LJ as Contest Manager at contest@qrparci.org and says 'Contest query - contact Contest Manager'; read from qrparci.org/contact-us/ on 2026-08-19. Ask for the RECURRENCE in the club's own wording rather than this year's dates, plus start/end in UTC, bands, modes, exchange, log format and deadline, and who may enter -- and ideally the last few years' dates, which is the independent check every other record in this catalog is held to. A reply is a citable primary source if it is recorded with the name and the date. A QRP Quarterly issue the club publishes itself would do equally well. STATUS 2026-08-19: THE EMAIL IS OUT. W4GGJ wrote to Larry Makowski W2LJ at contest@qrparci.org asking for the recurrence in the club's own wording, the UTC times, bands, modes, exchange, log format and deadline, and who may enter, plus the last two or three years' dates as the independent check. DO NOT SEND A SECOND ONE. When the reply arrives it IS the primary source: record it in each record's source_note with W2LJ's name and the date of the reply, set verified accordingly, and test the generated dates against whichever past years he gives.

The club publishes four DATES a year and no rule -- March 14, June 20, October 17, December 26 for 2026 -- and no ordinal fits all four, so the record holds exactly those and produces nothing for 2027 until the next list is read. THE ORGANISER IS AN ATTRIBUTION RATHER THAN A QUOTATION -- the rules page names no society at all, crediting only a wine sponsor for the awards, so 'RTTY Contesting' is the site that publishes and runs it. Same standing as the OK DX RTTY attribution and worth the same question. The site also carries an 'International FT Challenge', unread, which is the 2.

BLOCKED ON A RULES PAGE THAT SHIPS NO RULES, 2026-08-23. Everything needed to place it on a calendar is published and confirmed: 'taking place on the 4th full weekend of January', dates 'January 23rd & 24th, 2027', modes 'voice, CW, and digital transmissions' on 'HF, VHF, or UHF bands'. What is missing is the START AND END TIMES, the exchange and the log deadline -- and a contest record without a start time is not a record, so nothing is encoded rather than half-encoded with a guessed hour.

The rules live at winterfieldday.org/sop.php and that page carries 10 KB of HTML with 372 CHARACTERS OF VISIBLE TEXT: no iframe, no embed, no PDF link, no 'UTC' anywhere in the source. The content is loaded some other way or is simply not there. www. redirects to the apex, /rules.php 404s, and the site dropped the connection outright on an earlier attempt.

Worth one look in a browser -- if the page renders in Chrome but not in the fetcher, this is a five-minute fix and the same technique unblocks SRS's JavaScript-only pages listed in NEEDS_A_HUMAN. If it does not render there either, the page is broken and the WFDA is worth an email.

It is the owner's home state and this entry already named it first under local_priority, so it is the one record that does not reopen the sequencing argument below. Sponsor's own wording: 'Starts the last Saturday of April' -- a last-SATURDAY rule, not last-full-weekend -- two sessions with a night between them, and NO DIGITAL, which is unusual for a state party and worth knowing before filtering. The other ~45 remain not-started for the reason that follows, which has not changed. Roughly 45 US state QSO parties plus Canadian provincial parties. Each has its own sponsoring club and site. The State QSO Party Challenge (stateqsoparty.com) indexes them but is itself an aggregator -- use it only to locate sponsors, then source from each sponsor directly. region_map.$comment: Maps a contest record's `country` to the region used in coverage.by_region. Both engines read this rather than hard-coding a mapping. A country in the catalog that is missing here fails a test.

$region_map_note: OC is not an ISO country code. It is the code for a contest whose sponsor is a multi-national body inside one region -- currently only the Oceania DX Contest Committee, a joint VK/ZL committee. INTL is the same idea a level up, for a sponsor with no region at all. Neither is a country, and neither should be used where a national society owns the contest.

coverage.$comment: GENERATED by scripts/coverage.py from data/contests.seed.json. Do not hand-edit -- both test suites recompute it and fail on any drift, which is the point: this is the one block in the file that cannot go stale.

thin.$comment: Where the catalog is not a world calendar yet. `regions_with_nothing` is the headline: a region with zero contests is invisible to every operator in it, which is a worse failure than an unverified record.

engine_gaps.detail: CWops CWT runs weekly; SKCC Sprint, ARS Spartan Sprint, 4SQRP Second Sunday Sprint and NCCC Sprint run monthly. The old engine produced at most one occurrence per contest per year.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. Rule types `weekly` and `monthly_nth_weekday` added and expand() returns a list. These high-frequency contests are now a large share of the catalog's 648 occurrences for 2026.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL 10 GHz has two rounds; Stew Perry runs three or four times a year; EME has multiple weekends.
engine_gaps.fix: Currently handled by separate records per leg, which works but duplicates metadata. Consider a 'legs' array on one record.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL EME dates are set annually based on lunar conditions and have no fixed rule. NCJ publishes Sprint dates without a recurrence rule, and CQ publishes dates for all eight of its contests without one.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. Rule type `manual` takes an explicit date table. Note the CQ case is different and did NOT need it: CQ publishes no rule, but its published dates fit a stable recurrence, which is derivable and testable against eleven years of them. Prefer that over `manual` where the dates actually do follow a rule. The clearest instance found since is RAC Canada Winter (added 2026-08-17): eight dates from eight of RAC's own annual rules PDFs land on the fourth, third, third, third, fifth, third and fourth December Saturday -- and in 2026 on a Sunday. No ordinal fits, so 2027 onward is simply absent from the calendar rather than guessed, which is what `manual` is for.

engine_gaps.gap: Contests dated relative to a weekday near a fixed date
engine_gaps.detail: The WIA Remembrance Day Contest runs on the 'weekend in August closest to the 15th' -- neither an ordinal weekday nor a fixed date, and the two readings diverge every year the 15th is not itself a Saturday.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. Rule type `nearest_weekday` takes a month, a day and a weekday, and moves at most three days in whichever direction is shorter. It can never be ambiguous: a tie would need a distance of 3.5 days, which does not exist because seven is odd. All seven cases are pinned by test in both engines, against WIA's published 2023 (August 12) and 2026 (August 15) dates.

engine_gaps.gap: Weekly contests that run only in some months
engine_gaps.detail: NZART's ZL Autumn and Winter Sprints run 'each Tuesday in April and August' and on no other Tuesday. `weekly` covered the whole year and `composite` was the obvious workaround.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. `weekly` now takes the same optional `months` key `monthly_nth_weekday` already had. The composite workaround was tried first and rejected: it would have to name a fifth Tuesday, neither April nor August 2026 has one, and the sub-call raises rather than returning nothing -- so the whole contest would have vanished that year.

engine_gaps.detail: The old `local_time` flag conflated two opposite problems. Sponsor-anchored contests (4SQRP SSS, ARS Spartan Sprint) have exactly one correct UTC instant that moves an hour with DST; operator-anchored contests have none at all. This entry's own example was also wrong: ARRL moved 10 GHz off local time to fixed UTC and says so in the rules.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. `local_time` retired. Sponsor-anchored records carry an IANA `timezone` plus `wall_clock` time specs, resolved through stdlib `zoneinfo`. Operator-anchored records carry `local_rolling` and expose no UTC instant at all (start/end are None). Both DST edges pinned by test. Windows needs `tzdata`; see requirements.txt. NOTE: no catalog record is operator-anchored today -- the capability is tested against a synthetic definition so the next one found does not get a fabricated instant.

estimated_scope.$comment: Pre-research estimates, kept for planning only. Compare against `coverage`, which is generated. See counts_are_estimates.
estimated_scope.note: Reaching WA7BNM's ~500 requires the long tail of small regional and weekly events, which is where the remaining effort compounds. 309 well-sourced contests covers essentially everything an active contester would ever enter. Two of these estimates are known to be unreachable as written: QRP ARCI's 8 are blocked at source and SARL's 10 are behind a dead host, so ~18 of the 309 need a human before they need an engineer.
